title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. k is a principal ideal domain: the page writes n ∈ k−{0} and uses the gcd (m,n). The objects are '½-simplicial' (semi-simplicial) ∂-projective k-modules of finite type. Via the associated chain complex they become bounded complexes L. of finite free k-modules. The previous page decomposes every such object into indecomposables of three kinds:
- Λ^iΦ_*: the contractible complex k --id--> k in degrees i, i−1, i.e. the case n=1.
- L(i,n)_* (also written Φ(i,n)): the elementary complex k --n--> k in degrees i, i−1.
- Λ^iΨ_*: the 'sphere' k[i].
The stated programme (previous page, point 3) is to describe the additive category of these objects by computing all Hom groups between indecomposables. This page carries that out.

Step 1. A chain map L(i,n) → L. is determined by the image ξ_i of the generator in degree i. The image ξ_{i−1} in degree i−1 must satisfy dξ_i = nξ_{i−1}. Since L_{i−1} is torsion-free, ξ_{i−1} is determined by ξ_i. Hence
Hom(L(i,n), L.) ≅ d_i^{-1}(nL_{i−1}) ⊂ L_i.

Step 2. Apply this to L. = L(j,m):
- j ≠ i, i+1: the Hom is 0.
- j = i: the Hom is {λ ∈ k : mλ ∈ nk} = n'k ≅ k, with n' = n/(m,n).
- j = i+1: the Hom is k, generated by the composite L(i,n) → Λ^iΨ (projection onto the top degree) → L(i+1,m) (inclusion of the bottom degree).

Step 3. Special cases.
- End(L(i,n)) = k·id ≅ k. So each L(i,n) has endomorphism ring k and no nontrivial idempotents.
- End(Λ^iΦ) = k.
- Hom(Λ^iΦ, Λ^{i+1}Φ) = k·λ, where λ = T_∧ is the evident map.

Step 4. Maps to spheres.
- Hom(L(i,n), Λ^jΨ) = k if j = i and 0 otherwise.
- In particular Hom(Λ^iΦ, Λ^jΨ) is generated, for j = i, by the canonical projection Λ^iΦ → Λ^iΨ.

Step 5. Maps out of spheres. Hom(Λ^iΨ, L.) = Z_i(L.). This is free of rank equal to the number of summands having a cycle in degree i:
- the summands L(i+1,n) with n a non-unit (multiplicity h);
- the summands Λ^{i+1}Φ (multiplicity H);
- the spheres Λ^iΨ (multiplicity ν_i).
So Z_i(L.) ≅ k^{H_{i+1}+h_{i+1}+ν_i}.

The next page completes the table: Hom(Λ^iΨ, Λ^jΨ) and Hom(Λ^iΨ, Φ(j,n)). It also exhibits Φ(i,n) as the pushout of the extension Λ^iΦ along n·id on Λ^{i−1}Ψ.

The whole page is the 'quiver with relations' bookkeeping for bounded finite free complexes over a PID. It is preparatory to the 'dévissage' and the multiplicative structures named in the title.
errors: The exponent in Z_i(L.) ≅ k^{...} is transcribed as h_{i+1}+h_{i-1}+ν_i. A summand concentrated in degrees i−1, i−2 contributes nothing to Z_i. The correct count is the two kinds of (i+1,i)-summands plus ν_i, e.g. H_{i+1}+h_{i+1}+ν_i. The manuscript most likely has a primed or otherwise distinguished h_{i+1}; either way h_{i−1} is wrong.
Minor: the range '∀ i ≥ 0' for L(i,n) is inconsistent with the previous page, where L(i,n) is listed for i ≥ 1. For i = 0 the complex would sit in degrees 0, −1. This is a convention issue only.

The Hom groups computed are groups of chain maps (morphisms in the additive category), not homotopy classes. This is consistent with the stated aim, but Hom(Λ^iΦ, −) would vanish up to homotopy; the reader should keep this in mind.

ideas.what: Hom(L(i,n), L.) ≅ d^{-1}(nL_{i-1}) ⊂ L_i, i.e. the representing property of the elementary complex k --n--> k
ideas.modern_name: Mod-n disk / Moore-complex co-representability of elementary complexes

ideas.what: Complete table of Hom groups between the indecomposables k[i], k --n--> k[i], k --id--> k[i] of bounded finite free complexes over a PID (End = k, Hom between consecutive types ≅ k, gcd condition n' = n/(m,n))
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms between indecomposable objects in the category of perfect complexes over a PID (Krull–Schmidt-type description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; structure theorem for free chain complexes over a PID (Smith normal form)

ideas.what: Hom(Λ^iΨ, L.) = Z_i(L.) with rank given by the multiplicities of indecomposable summands
ideas.modern_name: Cycles functor co-represented by the sphere complex

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct, elementary computations of chain maps between the standard indecomposable free complexes over a PID. They are bookkeeping for a larger dévissage project. Nothing here is new to a specialist; the interest lies only in the larger, unpublished project on ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: Exponent of k in the last displayed formula: should read h_{i+1} + h'_{i+1} (or H_{i+1}+h_{i+1}) + ν_i, not h_{i+1}+h_{i−1}+ν_i.
The diagram labels below should read ξ_i and nξ_{i−1} (the images of the generators), with u_i, u_{i−1} the vertical maps.
'(donc un anneau de ... k-algèbres isomorphe à k comme)': roughly 'donc un anneau d'endomorphismes, isomorphe à k comme k-algèbre'.
'Φ(i,−)' subscripts: id_{L(i,n)} is written as id_{Φ(i,n)}. The notations L(i,n) and Φ(i,n) are used interchangeably.
